item.title: Even stupendous black holes can’t explain dark matter
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03386-4

The theoretical objects would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation if they were a source of the invisible force pulling together the galaxies.
item.dc:title: Even stupendous black holes can’t explain dark matter

item.title: Daily briefing: The big push to personalize psychiatry
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03531-z

A data-driven approach could match treatments to individuals with more precision. Plus, funders in Europe are backing preprint-led publishing and whether professors should care about student evaluations.
item.dc:title: Daily briefing: The big push to personalize psychiatry
item.dc:creator: Jacob Smith

item.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11181-4

Dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory.
item.dc:title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory

item.title: Daily briefing: The future of psychedelics
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03482-5

Despite setbacks, pharma companies are betting big on psychedelic drugs to treat mental-health conditions. Plus, longevity researchers are turning their attention to pets and how to keep tabs on the tools in your lab.
item.dc:title: Daily briefing: The future of psychedelics
